This variant refers to the initial phase of the coarse-to-fine method, specifically optimizing primary rays in GPU scheduling by using low-resolution sphere tracing for initial steps.
It is used when GPU occupancy is limited by the high iteration count of standard sphere tracing.
- **Time Complexity:** The splitting strategy reduces the number of expensive high-precision SDF evaluations for rays that are far from the surface.
By marching 3 steps at low resolution, rays cover significant distance with fewer texture/SDF lookups.
- **Memory Complexity:** Requires storing ray states for multiple resolution levels or reusing buffers.
- **When to use:** Rendering large implicit scenes with high coherence; when primary ray performance is the bottleneck.
- **When not to use:** Scenes with high-frequency details that are not captured at low resolutions; when exact surface intersection is required without post-processing.
It leverages the property that nearby rays march similarly, allowing information from coarse rays to guide fine rays.
